synthesis.body: `pack.schema.json` and `agentbundle.build.lint_packs` both ship inside the published package and run against third-party catalogues via `agentbundle validate` and `agentbundle catalogue lint`. Adding an editorial rule (a prose-length cap, a wording convention) to either one silently exports this repository's taste as a hard failure in someone else's build. Repo-only policy lints belong in `tools/` as a `lint-x.py` + `test-lint-x.py` pair, wired into BOTH `tools/repo/build_gate_chain.py` and `.github/workflows/build-check.yml` — `lint-ci-parity` fails if the two disagree, and it also needs a `STEP_DISPOSITION` entry naming the local target. The catalogue-curation guard (RFC-0059 D6) is what catches the mistake, but only after the fact: it refuses any changeset touching `packages/agentbundle/**` or `packs/credential-brokers/**` without an `Engine-Change-RFC:` trailer. Treat that refusal as a design signal, not an obstacle to route around with the trailer.

title: A house-style rule put in the shipped package becomes an adopter's build break
